Hands-on walkthrough: create orders and track fulfillment

html:
The deal is signed, the contract mastered, and now the revenue must actually materialize: this is the Orders & Fulfillment phase. It is where CPQ hands the commercial data to the operational side of the business — split the quote into orders, orchestrate the handoff to fulfillment systems, track provisioning, and sync the result back to your ERP. Together with Contracts it carries 15% of the Certified CPQ Specialist blueprint, and "Orders" appears again in the Revenue Cloud blueprint's Contracts and Orders domain (11%).

This guide covers order generation from quotes, order orchestration through OrderFulfillmentService, fulfillment status on the Order object, asset creation, and the integration heartbeat objects — the Revenue_Sync__e platform event and the OPR_-style sync state you keep on the quote with CPQ_Sync_Status__c.

Learning objectives

  • Explain how an approved, contracted quote becomes one or more orders and why segmentation matters.
  • Distinguish order types (new, amendment, renewal, cancellation) and map them to their quotes.
  • Track order progress with Order.Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, and ERP_Order_Number__c.
  • Orchestrate fulfillment with the OrderFulfillmentService Apex service.
  • Generate assets from fulfilled order lines so subscriptions become manageable entitlements.
  • Configure order synchronization to an ERP and watch the sync state on CPQ_Sync_Status__c.
  • Publish and consume Revenue_Sync__e platform events for decoupled external integrations.
  • Recognize where order data flows into billing and revenue recognition downstream.

From quote to order

An order is the operationalized form of a quote: the sellable lines CPQ has agreed with the customer, grouped for the teams that must ship or provision them. CPQ generates orders from a quote (typically a contracted quote) and lets you split one quote into several orders — a hardware bundle might produce a "Hardware" order for logistics, a "Services" order for the PS team, and a "Subscription" order for licensing.

Quote attributeEffect on orders
Approval_Status__c = ApprovedOrder generation is permitted
CPQ_Sync_Status__cSync state marker the automation updates
Lines grouped by order typeOne order per business function
Contract__c linkOrder inherits the master agreement

The order carries commercial truth forward: Order.Total_ARR__c reflects the recurring value of the lines being provisioned, and each order line memorializes the unit prices, the discount, and the subscription start/end negotiated on the quote.

text
Approved Quote
   |-- split by fulfillment type -->
   |   Order A: Hardware         (physical shipment)
   |   Order B: Implementation   (professional services)
   +-> Order C: Subscription     (recurring license)
💡
Tip: Segment orders by who fulfills them, not by how they were priced. Segregation lowers integration complexity because each consuming system sees only the lines it is responsible for.

Order types and their lifecycles

Every order deserves to be tied back to a source so your reporting can say why an order exists. The academy model keeps discrimination in the source quote (Is_Renewal__c) and the order attributes themselves:

Order typeSourceWhat it does
New businessStandard quoteFirst-time provisioning
AmendmentAmendment quoteAdds/removes lines mid-term
RenewalRenewal quote (Is_Renewal__c = true)Re-commits the recurring term
CancellationChurn quoteTakes value off the books

Lifecycle-wise an order runs through statuses that the fulfillment team owns: Open → In Fulfillment → Fulfilled → (partially) → Closed. On the academy model the three fields to keep in sync are Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, and — once your ERP responds — ERP_Order_Number__c:

soql
SELECT Id, Name, Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c,
       ERP_Order_Number__c, Total_ARR__c
FROM Order
ORDER BY CreatedDate DESC

Order orchestration and fulfillment

OrderFulfillmentService is the academy's orchestrator. It owns the transitions of an order through fulfillment and knows the minimal set of data each downstream system needs. A typical flow:

  1. Validate the order is in a state that allows fulfillment (Open).
  2. Push the order lines to the fulfillment/ERP system via the Revenue_Sync__e platform event.
  3. On a successful response, stamp Fulfillment_Date__c, set the ERP reference in ERP_Order_Number__c, and move Fulfillment_Status__c to Fulfilled.
  4. On failure, retry with backoff and leave the order in In Fulfillment so an operator can intervene.
apex
public class OrderFulfillmentService {
    public static void markFulfilled(Order o, String erpNumber) {
        o.Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Fulfilled';
        o.Fulfillment_Date__c   = System.today();
        o.ERP_Order_Number__c   = erpNumber;
        update o;
    }
}

The orchestration layer is where you enforce the "no surprises" rule: an order for a Mastered contract belongs on the contract's amended terms, and an order flagged as a renewal must not be shipped like net-new business.

Assets: fulfillment that becomes manageable entitlements

For subscription and consumption businesses, an order line that gets fulfilled stops being a line and becomes an asset — a provisioned entitlement the business can see, amend, renew, and co-terminate. In legacy CPQ this is SBQQ__Subscription__c/SBQQ__Asset__c; in Revenue Cloud / RLM, asset lifecycle management is a first-class platform domain.

From order lineAsset carries
QuantityProvisioned units
Unit price / ARRRecognizable recurring value
Subscription start/endRenewal and recognition timing
ProductEligibility for future upgrades

Assets are the bridge objects: billing consumes them to make schedules, contracts reference them for renewal staging, and recognition keys off their timing. If the contract was the deal's legal snapshot, the asset is its living operational state.

ERP synchronization and the sync status field

The order does double duty: a CRM record and a contract with the ERP. Sync failures are normal in real integrations, so the design keeps state explicit. CPQ_Sync_Status__c on the quote and Fulfillment_Status__c on the order carry the operational state, while Revenue_Sync__e carries the message.

json
{
  "Source_Object__c": "Order",
  "Direction__c": "Outbound",
  "Integration_Type__c": "OrderFulfillment",
  "Endpoint__c": "https://erp.example.com/api/orders",
  "Correlation_Id__c": "ORD-0000123",
  "Retry_Count__c": 0,
  "Status__c": "Pending"
}

A clean sync pattern is outbox-style: when a quote/order transitions, capture the payload and the target in a platform event; the subscriber posts to the ERP, and on success flips the status. Batching and idempotency keys (Correlation_Id__c) make the retry logic safe — re-posting a fulfilled order is far worse than a stubborn one that never shipped.

apex
// Publish an order-fulfillment event to the outbound queue
public static void publishOrderSync(Order o) {
    List<Revenue_Sync__e> events = new List<Revenue_Sync__e>();
    events.add(new Revenue_Sync__e(
        Source_Object__c  = 'Order',
        Payload__c        = JSON.serialize(o),
        Direction__c      = 'Outbound',
        Endpoint__c       = calloutConfig.Endpoint,
        Correlation_Id__c = o.Id,
        Status__c         = 'Pending'
    ));
    EventBus.publish(events);
}

Where orders connect downstream

Orders are not the end; they are the hand-off. Billing needs the fulfilled subscription to build a schedule, revenue recognition needs the schedule timing to split value across periods, and renewal needs the asset to stage the next opportunity. The academy data model makes the links explicit: Revenue_Schedule__c carries Order__c alongside Contract__c and Account__c, so a single schedule record can answer "what am I billing, for which order, under which contract, and to whom."

That connectivity is also why order hygiene matters so much: a stray unfulfilled order corrupts recognition, billing, and renewal in one stroke. Fulfillment is the moment operational reality joins the commercial plan — do not proceed until the order is true.

Hands-on walkthrough: create orders and track fulfillment

This walkthrough uses the academy data model with OrderFulfillmentService and the Revenue_Sync__e platform event.

  1. Confirm you have a mastered contract generated from an approved quote (from the Contracts phase).
  2. Create three orders from the quote's lines — Hardware, Services, and Subscription — each with Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Open' and Total_ARR__c populated from its lines.
apex
List<Order> orders = new List<Order>{
    new Order(Name = 'ORD-HW-001',   Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Open', Total_ARR__c = 0),
    new Order(Name = 'ORD-SVC-001',  Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Open', Total_ARR__c = 0),
    new Order(Name = 'ORD-SUB-001',  Fulfillment_Status__c = 'Open', Total_ARR__c = 24000)
};
  1. Publish a Revenue_Sync__e event for the subscription order with Endpoint__c pointing at your lab's mock ERP and Correlation_Id__c = Ord.Id.
apex
EventBus.publish(new Revenue_Sync__e(
    Source_Object__c  = 'Order',
    Payload__c        = JSON.serialize(orders[2]),
    Direction__c      = 'Outbound',
    Integration_Type__c = 'OrderFulfillment',
    Correlation_Id__c = orders[2].Id,
    Status__c         = 'Pending'
));
  1. Simulate the ERP response: call OrderFulfillmentService.markFulfilled(order, 'ERP-9001') and confirm the order moved to Fulfilled with today's Fulfillment_Date__c and the ERP number stamped.
  2. Create an asset for each fulfilled subscription line from the order, carrying quantity, unit price, and the subscription start/end so billing has a source record.
  3. Query the Order table and confirm the tree: Open orders still lack ERP_Order_Number__c, fulfilled ones are complete.
soql
SELECT Name, Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, ERP_Order_Number__c
FROM Order
WHERE Name LIKE 'ORD-%'
  1. Publish the inbound ack (set Direction__c = 'Inbound', Status__c = 'Success') and confirm CPQ_Sync_Status__c on the source quote moved to Synced.
  2. Verify the subscription order's Total_ARR__c is linked into Revenue_Schedule__c records (via Order__c) ready for the Billing & Revenue phase.

Common pitfalls

  • Generating orders before approval — an unapproved quote seeding orders bypasses governance; always gate on Approval_Status__c.
  • One mega-order for everything — mash-ups force downstream teams to reconcile lines they don't own; split by fulfillment function.
  • Fulfilled-then-retry loops — without Correlation_Id__c idempotency, a retried callback duplicates the fulfillment.
  • Ignoring the amendment path — mid-term changes must flow through a new (amendment) quote and order, not a hand-edited order.
  • Assets that no one creates — unfulfilled subscription lines mean no assets, meaning no billing schedule; asset creation belongs in the fulfillment routine.
  • Letting CPQ_Sync_Status__c and order status drift — the quote sync marker and the order fulfillment state must move together or reports contradict the ERP.

Key takeaways

  • Orders operationalize the approved quote: segment by who fulfills, tie each order to its source, and carry Total_ARR__c forward.
  • Fulfillment_Status__c, Fulfillment_Date__c, and ERP_Order_Number__c are the trinity that proves an order really shipped.
  • Assets turn fulfilled lines into manageable entitlements and are the bridge to billing and renewal.
  • The Revenue_Sync__e platform event with a correlation key makes ERP integration decoupled and retry-safe.
  • Revenue schedules key off Order__c and Contract__c, so order hygiene determines the accuracy of everything downstream.
